notes: Sweep 2026-10-31, skill condition: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier; every assistant message that carries a model in each transcript carries the tier's model. Every result.json records head 0814e8d (0814e8d95b3cfb385a030184ee729f5f620fcde3) with uncommitted false and skill_hash 388693662c84a3c1234ff9d36d4172a43a0ba572981ae0b2d02592f2d91ffab3, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show reads of SKILL.md and references/ex_unit.md in all five (haiku-2 also printed SKILL.md with cat and sed before its Read calls) and of references/processes.md in opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not haiku-1 or haiku-2, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is met in 3 of 5. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the eleven rules this case's index rows name, four changed or are new, and three of them gained test-writing in their row since the 2026-10-23 sweep, which graded eight. "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" is new, with no earlier verdict. "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" is rewritten. "Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" has a rewritten first bullet and an example. In ex_unit.md, "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" adds one sentence on condition blocks. The other seven (Open a module, Run tests concurrently, Assert with patterns, Wait for messages, Start processes, Replace dependencies, Use setup) are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard; the 2026-10-31-check grading of the same shapes (at 551e3ab plus the uncommitted Readability rewrite) is followed for the three new rows.

"One expression per line, and tabular clauses" (new): clean in 5 of 5. Deciding sentence: "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces." Constructs: opus-1 lines 17-18 defp delivery_result("bounced@example.com"), do: {:error, :bounced} / defp delivery_result(_to), do: :ok, two rows of one mapping with one fallback row, a table under "each row is one alternative of the same decision or mapping ... at most one final row catches what did not match"; sonnet-2 line 10 def registry, do: @registry; the one clause :stop -> :ok in every run's receive (opus-1 209, haiku-1 184, haiku-2 158, sonnet-1 156, sonnet-2 144); one-line fns with one expression on body lines (haiku-1 49, haiku-2 153, sonnet-1 141), which the rule's own fn sentence keeps on one line; every fn holding a receive puts it on the lines below (opus-1 207-211, haiku-1 182-186, sonnet-2 142-146), per "Those go on the lines below the head"; every test, setup and helper with several steps has them below its head. haiku-1 line 43 is a head mix format would spread (the file fails --check-formatted there); it holds one selection with its body below, so it is counted under Before you finish, not here, as 2026-10-31-check did with a spread head.

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (changed): clean in 5 of 5. opus-1 lines 17-18 and sonnet-2 line 10 are decided by "A `do:` body is one expression on the head's line: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not."; opus-1's two clauses are also covered by "A multi-clause function need not be a table to keep `do:` clauses". Bodies holding a fn or a receive are blocks in every run (opus-1 206-214, haiku-1 181-187, haiku-2 152-160, sonnet-1 139-158, sonnet-2 140-153 and 184-194), per "or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is" and the receive named in that sentence; sonnet-2's two stop/2 clauses are both blocks with a blank line between them. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 have no do: at all, graded clean as 2026-10-31-check graded such files. No run has a for, a one-line if/else, a capture, or a case, so the for, if and capture sentences have nothing to apply to.

"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" (changed): the deciding sentence would be "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short", but no file contains |>, so the rule is not exercised in 5 of 5, as in 2026-10-31-check.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (changed in its describe half). The new sentence that decides condition blocks is "A block named after a condition, or after a requirement where the project asks for that, still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict", read with the case's own example ("when a subscriber exits", not "exits"). Condition blocks: opus-1 129, haiku-1 125, haiku-2 97 and sonnet-1 117 "when a subscribed process exits"; sonnet-2 139 "when a subscribed process has exited"; each names the situation the rule's ExUnit example names, clean. Function-plus-condition blocks (haiku-2 47 "publish/3 to a process subscriber", 63 "publish/3 to an email subscriber") name one function, clean as before. The one violation is in the unchanged sentence "A block that joins two functions (`describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2"`) no longer says which one a failure is about": haiku-1 line 55 describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2" do, the rule's own example word for word. Test names (unchanged half), per run: opus-1 16, haiku-1 17, haiku-2 13, sonnet-1 14, sonnet-2 15, all state a value or an effect; no "returns :ok", "works" or "succeeds" name in any run. Borderline names kept clean as in every earlier sweep: haiku-1 117 "leaves the server running when the topic has no subscribers", sonnet-1 108 "does nothing for a topic nobody subscribed to" and 134 "keeps the server running", sonnet-2 176 "keeps the server running". sonnet-1 124 "stops notifying it, and still mails the others" claims more than its body checks (nothing refutes a notification to the dead pid), an accuracy problem, not the forbidden shape. Rule result: 1 of 5 violates (haiku-1).

"Use setup for shared data" (unchanged): opus-1 is graded violated, a judgment call on a shape no earlier sweep has. Two tests take the whole context and match the setup's data in the body: line 172 test "removes both entries of a process that subscribed twice", context do / line 173 %{server: server, subscriber: subscriber} = context, and lines 185-186 the same. The rule says "Return data from `setup` as a map and match what each test needs in its head", and the case's check says tests match the map in their heads; matching it on the first body line instead, apparently to keep the head under 98 characters, is not what the rule asks. This differs from the context reads graded clean before (2026-10-23 haiku-1 line 164, and sonnet-2 lines 42-43 here: Module.concat(context.module, "#{context.test} without mailer")), which read the test's identity keys to build a name, the shape the Start processes rule's own example writes; opus-1 pulls the setup's own data out in the body. The same line 173 is not counted under "Assert with patterns": its keys are guaranteed by the describe's setup, so it is a destructure that cannot fail, like {result, log} = with_log(...) in that rule. If the ruling goes the other way, opus-1 is clean on every graded rule. The other four runs return a map from every setup and match it in every test head.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": haiku-1 lines 49-51 ({result, _log} = with_log(fn -> start_supervised({Subscriptions, name: name}) end) / assert {:error, _reason} = result) call start_supervised/1 but leave the reason open, violated on "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason.", the same shape and judgment as 2026-10-23 haiku-1 line 166. sonnet-2 line 47 assert {:error, {{%KeyError{key: :mailer}, _stacktrace}, _child}} = start_supervised(spec) matches the reason, clean as every earlier sweep graded this match. No run calls start_link. haiku-1 lines 202-221 put the one default-name test in its own async: false module (line 210 start_supervised!({Subscriptions, mailer: TestMailer})), not counted under this rule or the concurrency rule, as 2026-10-22-c and later sweeps treated default-name tests in an async: false module. Subscribers: opus-1 start_supervised!({Task, wait_for_stop}) (line 213) and haiku-2 start_supervised!({Task, fn -> wait_for_stop() end}) (line 153); haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 bare spawn/1, clean as before.

"Wait for messages, not for time": every :DOWN pattern matches the reason the test caused: opus-1 line 189 :normal and its helper at line 217, assert_receive {:trace, ^server, :receive, {:DOWN, _ref, :process, ^subscriber, ^reason}}, which traces the server (line 202 :erlang.trace(server, true, [:receive])) so the test waits for the server's own :DOWN with the pinned reason (:normal, :killed or :noproc) before calling subscribers/2; haiku-1 lines 192 :normal and 198 :killed; haiku-2 lines 105 :normal and 116, 128, 142 :killed; sonnet-1 line 149 :killed; sonnet-2 lines 187 :normal and 193 :killed. Every refute_received or refute_receive follows a synchronous call (opus-1 :sys.get_state at 88; haiku-1 :sys.get_state at 111; haiku-2 subscribers/2 at 58; sonnet-1 at 102 and 110; sonnet-2 at 121) or an assert_receive (sonnet-2 135). No Process.sleep anywhere; haiku-1 lines 121 and 177, sonnet-1 135 and sonnet-2 180 assert Process.alive?(server) once, not polling, as 2026-10-31-check graded.

The other graded rules are clean in 5 of 5. All five use async: true in the main module with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing test mailer (@behaviour Notify.Mailer, @impl true) that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name; no Process.register, application env, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. haiku-1's second module is async: false only for the default-name test (line 203 comment: The default name is global), a named singleton the rule allows. Every == has the call on the left; no elem/2, no bind-then-==; opus-1 112-113 and sonnet-2 81-82 bind expected = [...] and compare the call to it whole. Directive order: use then alias in all five, with haiku-1 line 23 import ExUnit.CaptureLog between them in the right place.

Outside this case's list: haiku-1 line 43 test "registers the server under the :name option", %{server: server, module: module, test: test} do is 104 characters and fails mix format --check-formatted (mix format spreads the map over five lines); the transcript shows the session ran its tests but never ran mix format, counted under Before you finish (step 1) as earlier sweeps counted unformatted files. "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" (its assertion sentence changed: an expected map or list that mix format spreads over lines inside an assertion is bound first as expected): no run spreads an expected literal inside an assertion; sonnet-1 lines 65-66 assert Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") == / ["bob@example.com", self(), "ann@example.com"] is a formatter wrap after == with the list on one line, not counted, as 2026-10-31-check graded the same sonnet-2 shape; opus-1 112-113 and sonnet-2 81-82 already bind expected. Comments in all five give reasons (for example opus-1 198-200, haiku-2 150-151). Nothing else found.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings or log output (opus-1 16 tests, haiku-1 17, haiku-2 13, sonnet-1 14, sonnet-2 15). mix format --check-formatted passes for opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and fails for haiku-1 at line 43, confirming format_ok in result.json. Against 2026-10-23 (skill): opus goes from clean on every rule to one judged violation of Use setup (a new shape); haiku again breaks Start processes with an open start-failure reason (haiku-1 both times) and again breaks Group tests, this time with a two-function describe instead of a returns :ok name; sonnet goes from one returns :ok name (sonnet-2 line 108 then) to clean on every rule. The three rules newly graded in this case (One expression, do:, pipelines) are clean or not exercised in every run.
